    "RH": "In the fixed configuration the AIM capability grant (web:read, flight:search, chat:respond) is enforced in code at the tool-call boundary, outside model output, and the outbound http:post is denied; the enforcement channel is not reachable by the agent and the fixed-binding isolation is shown in the code.",
    "ES": "The tool surface on this path is a fixed, allowlisted capability binding enforced at the egress boundary rather than dynamic or unvetted extension.",
    "CVSS": "The attacker is the poisoned-page author who must first get the traveler to ask FlightBot to fetch the page (UI:A), but the AIM twin denies the outbound wallet exfiltration at the egress boundary, so the traveler's stored wallet never leaves and no confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact remains in the vulnerable agent process; the traveler already owns the wallet, and the residual path is only the injection landing in context."

      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:493-513",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1128-1145",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/README.md:26"

  "confidence": {
    "LC": "high",
    "CP": "medium",
    "AP": "medium",
    "RH": "medium",

    "CVSS": "medium"
  },

    "locus": null
  },

  "technical_impact": "Partial",
  "technical_impact_rationale": "The indirect injection still lands in the agent's context and the wallet summary is read, but the capability boundary blocks the outbound exfiltration, so no data leaves the agent process.",
  "applicability_as_implemented": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "confidence": "high",
    "rationale": "In the default simulated mode no LLM runs; the fetch, injection detection, and callback steps are a deterministic scripted path in index.js, so no model directs goals or selects tool actions."

Hmm, is the reward channel reachable? Enforcement is deterministic code, not model-controlled. I'll set reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=true → RH=N.
